title: Autoscaler provisioning feedback-loop: guardrails and mitigation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a regional traffic surge on 2025-02-17 we observed an autoscaling provisioning feedback loop that resulted in substantial over-provisioning of Dedicated capacity in us-east-1. The root cause traces to a combination of: (1) a recent change to the provisioning estimator’s smoothing parameters (canary rollout), (2) a new warm-pool pre-warming hook that reported readiness before model KV cache was fully seeded, and (3) a latency-based scaling metric (P99 request latency) that was noisy during warm-up. These factors produced a positive feedback loop: early instances reported degraded latency -> estimator over-inferred required capacity -> controller ramped more replicas and pre-warmed warm-pools -> synthetic/prewarm traffic reduced observed latency for warmed replicas but not user-facing ones, confusing the estimator and causing repeated scale cycles.

Impact:
- Temporary over-commit of ~120% above expected capacity in us-east-1 (3 hours) causing elevated cost and throttling of background maintenance tasks in other clusters.
- Increased tail latency for some customer requests due to node churn and frequent model cache reloads.
- Several customers saw degraded throughput for smaller bursty endpoints (medium/high impact for a subset of Dedicated customers).

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-17 02:08 UTC: Canary rollout of estimator smoothing change (runtime-1.19-canary) enabled for 10% of traffic.
- 2025-02-17 02:22 UTC: Traffic spike from partner integration (unexpected 6x) begins.
- 2025-02-17 02:25 UTC: Warm-pool prewarm hook returns readiness before KV cache population completed.
- 2025-02-17 02:30–05:15 UTC: Autoscaler repeatedly increased replicas; scale-down suppressed due to short cooldown combined with warm-pool jitter.
- 2025-02-17 05:25 UTC: On-call notice; mitigation actions applied (roll back canary, temporary scale-up cap, disable warm-pool prewarm reporting).
- 2025-02-17 06:12 UTC: Observed stabilization and progressive scale-down; post-incident analysis started.

Root cause analysis (concise):
1) Estimator smoothing change: The new exponential smoothing alpha was reduced to prioritize recent measurements. That made the estimator highly reactive to short-lived spikes. The change was rolled out without a synthetic load test that reproduced warm-up characteristics of model serving (large KV cache cost).
2) Warm-pool readiness semantics: Prewarm hook returned success when the container process was responsive, not when model cache priming completed. The readiness signal therefore underrepresented user-facing latency during initial traffic.
3) Metric selection & observability: Using raw P99 latency from edge proxies as the scaling signal amplified noise during warm-up. There was insufficient fusion with queue length and CPU utilization signals that would have provided context.
4) No scale-up guardrail: There was no hard cap on scale-up rate for the Dedicated pool; autoscaler could provision many replicas within minutes when estimator signaled a sudden need.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Rolled back estimator smoothing change to previous stable alpha (runtime-1.18 config).
- Temporarily disabled warm-pool readiness reporting and set warm-pool size to fixed minimum for the region.
- Added a temporary scale-up cap (max 2x in 10 minutes) for affected Dedicated pools.
- Notified impacted customers and created follow-up support tickets.

Action items and owners (concrete, prioritized):
1) Implement scale-up rate limiter and global scale cap per-pool (owner: Miguel Santos, estimate: 3).
2) Redefine warm-pool readiness semantics: readiness must include KV cache seed completion or a measured user-request latency check (owner: Priya Desai, estimate: 5).
3) Add multi-signal scaling policy: fuse P99 latency + queue depth + CPU/gpu utilization with voting logic and hysteresis (owner: Linh Tran, estimate: 8, dependency: infra-metrics-schema).
4) Add synthetic warmup suite to CI that reproduces KV cache costs and run it on every estimator change (owner: Asha Patel, estimate: 3).
5) Create a canary gating checklist for estimator/tuning rollouts including a dedicated traffic replay test (owner: SRE team lead - Nora Fitzgerald, estimate: 2).
6) Dashboard & alerting: build a composite dashboard for scale-loop signals and an alert when scale events exceed a threshold within a sliding window (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 2, release: runtime-1.19).
7) Update runbooks/runplay: add explicit troubleshooting steps for provisioning feedback loops and include rollback & customer-communication play (owner: Miguel Santos, estimate: 1).
8) Capacity economics review: quantify cost impact and propose credit/compensation where warranted (owner: Finance Ops - Rachel Bloom, estimate: 2).

Dependencies:
- infra-metrics-schema change to include warmed_cache_ready and pool_provision_rate (dependency: ENG-891000).
- SRE team coordination for canary traffic replays and game day (dependency: SRE-ops).

Acceptance criteria for completion:
- Scale-up rate limiter merged and in canary for 10% traffic without regressions.
- Warm-pool readiness semantics updated and validated by synthetic warmup suite.
- Multi-signal scaling policy implemented in staging and demonstrated to prevent >30% overshoot under synthetic spikes.
- Runbook updated and incident retro published to Confluence.

Postmortem docs and artifacts:
- Grafana composite dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/scale-loop/scale-loop-overview
- Incident Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01INCIDENTS/p1676620000000
- PR with rollback and hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
- Draft postmortem (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INC/2025-02-17+Autoscale+Feedback+Loop

Notes and trade-offs discussed:
- Increasing smoothing window reduces reactivity to real traffic pattern shifts; multi-signal policy preferred to blunt parameter tuning as the only fix.
- Warm-pool benefits (reduced cold starts) must be balanced against accurate readiness reporting; seed-aware readiness is a small cost but high reliability win.
- Rate-limiting scale-ups reduces rapid capacity availability but prevents costly oscillations; we will combine limits with fast warm-paths to preserve latency SLOs.

Next checkpoints:
- 2025-03-03: Merge PR for scale-up limiter into canary (owner: Miguel Santos).
- 2025-03-10: Synthetic warmup suite integrated into estimator CI (owner: Asha Patel).
- 2025-03-15: Postmortem review with Engineering + SRE + Product; decide long-term rollout plan.
